title: Performance Engineering
opening: A useful session begins with the ability you want, the part currently limiting it, and an attempt that can show what to work on next.

labels.taskIntro: A packing line needs to assemble complete field packs. Work out the session target from the stock and per-pack requirements. The material with the fewest possible complete packs limits the run.
labels.objectivePrompt: Which answer will you practice producing accurately?
labels.attemptPrompt: Select the answer for the chosen capability, then check it.
labels.sourceSequenceIntro: Preparation changes the conditions for the work; it does not replace the attempt or its feedback. Use the result to choose an adjustment, then check later whether the ability still holds in the setting where it matters.

field-pack.title: Field packs
field-pack.prompt: Each pack needs 3 cards, 2 tags, and 4 clips.

workshop-kit.title: Workshop kits
workshop-kit.prompt: Each kit needs 4 cloths, 3 buckles, and 2 tags.

objective.title: Find the number of complete packs
Find the limiting material
objective.description: Practice identifying which stock sets that output.

preparation.title: Write stock ÷ per pack
preparation.description: Use the ratio prompt before choosing an answer.

preparation.title: Start without the ratio prompt
preparation.description: Choose an answer without the formula being shown.

feedback.title: Show the component calculations
feedback.description: Inspect each material's complete-pack capacity and the limiting row.

feedback.title: Show the result first
feedback.description: See whether the answer works, then decide what to adjust.

practice.prediction: What single capability will your next session develop, and what result will let you inspect an attempt at it?
practice.observation: If your preparation is ready but you have not tried the skill, what can the first performance attempt show you that preparation cannot? Use the attempt above in your answer.
practice.comparison: Why does each part of your session exist? Connect the target, limiter, preparation, attempt, feedback, adjustment, and later check to the result you want.
practice.result: What would a later task need to show before you could say the ability improved and remained available? What did this checked attempt show, and what remains untested?
practice.revision: If the session gets more elaborate but performance or retention does not improve, what would you simplify or change? What observation would lead you to that change?
practice.step: Plan a session for a movement skill using the same target, attempt, and feedback logic. What task conditions matter, and where will you later check the ability?
